sections.content: You know the words for "maybe" and the mood that goes with them from B2 Unit 3 (*a lo mejor*, *quizás*, *es evidente que*, *no es seguro que*), *dudo que* from B1 Unit 13 and hedging from B2 Unit 21. Together they form a scale from certain to doubtful. This lesson adds one more way to say you are sure.

sections.title: From sure to doubtful
rows: No cabe duda de que el plan funcionará.
There is no doubt that the plan will work.
Es evidente que el plan funciona.
It is clear that the plan works.
A lo mejor el plan funciona.
Perhaps the plan works (I am less sure).
I doubt that the plan works.

sections.content: *No cabe duda de que* is a strong, formal way to say "there is no doubt". It takes the indicative, because you present the fact as certain. In the same way *no dudo que* takes the indicative: *No dudo que viene*. Doubting is the other side: *dudo que* and *no es seguro que* take the subjunctive. The rule is the one from B2 Unit 3: a fact you present as certain takes the indicative, and a doubt takes the subjunctive.

In an essay, choose one point on the scale for each claim and keep to it. A text where everything is "certain" sounds pushy, and one where everything is "maybe" says nothing. Save *no cabe duda de que* for the one claim you really want to defend.
